6	    "finding": "👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Edit rollback leaves a newly written identity.json when the folder had none before**\n\nWhen the registry write fails, the rollback only restores the folder's file if `previous.kind === \"ok\"`. Take a pending entry whose folder is reachable but has no `identity.json` (`previous` is missing). `edit` writes a fresh identity at line 581 with the entry's id and the new name. If `update` then throws, that file stays on disk. The next probe finds an identity with the matching id and adopts it, so the change that was refused shows up again. Calling `removeIdentity(entry.path)` in the non-ok case would undo it the way `create`'s `undo` does.\n\n<!-- wachi:finding -->",
7	    "replies": [
8	      {
9	        "author": "csdev19",
10	        "body": "Fixed in 886d67f0: the rollback also calls `removeIdentity` when the folder had no file. In practice the probe at the start of `edit` rewrites a missing identity first, so `previous` is normally `ok` by then; I added a test for that real path (the old file is back after a failed registry write) and kept the `absent` branch as the guard for the race."
11	      }

If the payload is malformed only in its color, it should report `invalid-color`, which `WorkspaceCreateRefusal` already has. Otherwise the renderer would flag the name field. Splitting the check into two would report the right field.\n\n<!-- wachi:finding -->",

30	    "finding": "👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Edit does not re-check name uniqueness inside the locked write, unlike create**\n\n`create` re-runs `validateWorkspaceName` inside `update`, so two concurrent creates cannot take the same name (line 515). `edit` validates only once, at line 540, before several awaits (the probe, `readIdentity`, `writeIdentity`). So two concurrent edits, or an edit racing a create, can both pass the check and leave two workspaces with the same name. The same `NameTakenError` re-check inside the `update` callback would close this gap.\n\n<!-- wachi:finding -->",
31	    "replies": [
32	      {
33	        "author": "csdev19",
34	        "body": "Fixed in 886d67f0: `edit` now re-runs the name check inside the locked `update`, throws `NameTakenError` and reports `name-taken`, undoing the identity write. New test: two concurrent edits to \"Same\" and \"same\" leave exactly one winner and the loser's `identity.json` untouched."
35	      }
36	    ]

40	    "path": "apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/registry.ts",
41	    "line": 809,
42	    "finding": "👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Change folder… refuses the moved folder of a `pendingInit` workspace, which is the case it is meant to fix (confidence medium)**\n\n`open()` registers the migrated Default workspace with `pendingInit` when the old `vaultDirectory` is unplugged at upgrade (lines 298-303). In that case no `identity.json` was ever written to that folder. Suppose the drive comes back at a different mount path. That is the case the not-connected notice's button exists for. The folder has `.kaipu/` sidecars and no identity, so `checkRelocate` reaches line 809 and returns `has-items-no-identity`. The user is told the folder \"isn't one of your workspaces\" and cannot repoint it.\n\nThe same rule hits a `pendingInit` entry whose moved folder already holds an identity with another id. Line 802 refuses it as `different`, but `availability` adopts that id at lines 678-687.\n\nA possible fix: when `entry.pendingInit` is set, accept a folder with no identity (the probe writes it later). For a folder with another workspace's identity, apply the same `pendingInit && !this.get(identity.id)` adoption rule that `availability` uses.\n\n<!-- wachi:finding -->",
43	    "replies": [
44	      {
45	        "author": "csdev19",
46	        "body": "> [!NOTE]\n> 🤖 **Claude Sonnet 5.5 responding on behalf of Cristian Sotomayor**\n\nHalf real. Fixed in 85200ab3: a `pendingInit` workspace (never got an `identity.json`) now accepts a moved folder that has Kaipu items and no identity, and the probe after the move writes the identity under the registered id. Other workspaces still refuse such a folder, as before. Not changed: the `pendingInit` entry whose moved folder already holds another id. Adopting that id changes `activeId` and `legacyCloudOwnerId`, which belongs in the probe, not in `relocate`; it needs both a drive that moved and an identity written by another Mac in between. Noted as a follow-up."

53	    "line": 131,
54	    "finding": "👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Relocating the active workspace throws away a pending quiet capture that could still be saved (confidence medium)**\n\n`relocateActive` calls `dropPendingCaptures()`, which dismisses the capture toast and clears the retained PNG (`apps/kaipu-record/src/main/index.ts:975-978`). That makes sense for a switch, where the capture belongs to the old workspace. After a relocate the workspace id stays the same, and the toast's save goes through `saveCaptureToWorkspace(workspaceId, …)` → `workspaceGate().runActive(workspaceId, …)` (`screenshot-save.ts:87-95`). That save would still succeed and land in the new folder. As written, an unsaved screenshot disappears without explanation when the user picks the workspace's new folder. Consider leaving `dropPendingCaptures` out of the relocate transaction.\n\n<!-- wachi:finding -->",
55	    "replies": [
56	      {
57	        "author": "csdev19",
58	        "body": "> [!NOTE]\n> 🤖 **Claude Sonnet 5.5 responding on behalf of Cristian Sotomayor**\n\nOut of scope here: dropping pending captures is part of the relocate transaction on purpose (`relocate.test.ts` pins the order), and the case needs a capture toast alive during the few seconds of a folder change. Keeping the saved-to-new-folder behavior would also need a check that a retained capture has no path into the old folder. Noted as a follow-up."
59	      }
60	    ]

63	    "comment_id": 4439290177,
64	    "path": "apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/relocate.ts",
65	    "line": 46,
66	    "finding": "👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Picking the active workspace's current folder still runs the full transaction (confidence high)**\n\n`checkRelocate` returns `{ ok: true }` when the picked folder is the one already registered: identity id matches (line 802), or same path (line 808). For the active workspace, `relocateWorkspace` still calls `relocateActive`. That asks every window to prepare (an unsaved editor gets the Save/Discard/Cancel question), bumps the generation (routes remount) and drops pending captures, all for a no-op. Picking the same folder is easy to do, because the picker opens at `dirname(entry.path)` (`index.ts:331`). Returning early with the unchanged entry when `samePath(entry.path, chosen)` would avoid that.\n\n<!-- wachi:finding -->",
67	    "replies": [
68	      {
69	        "author": "csdev19",
70	        "body": "> [!NOTE]\n> 🤖 **Claude Sonnet 5.5 responding on behalf of Cristian Sotomayor**\n\nReal, fixed in 4a300696: when the picked folder is the one the workspace already points at, `relocateWorkspace` returns the unchanged entry before the transaction, so no window is asked to save, no capture is dropped and the generation stays. The caller's probe still runs. Test: same folder on the active workspace leaves the log empty and the generation at 1."
71	      }
72	    ]

77	    "line": 43,
78	    "finding": "👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Picking the current folder still shows \"now points to the new folder\" (confidence high)**\n\nThe new early return gives `{ ok: true, entry: current }` when the picked folder is the one the workspace already uses. `relocateFolder` passes that on as `ok: true` (`index.ts:340-349`). Both the dialog and Settings then call `onRelocated`, which always shows `folderChanged`, \"Done. {name} now points to the new folder.\" (`workspaces-context.tsx:165-167`). That case is easy to hit, because the picker opens at `dirname(entry.path)` (`index.ts:331`). The user is told the folder changed when nothing did. You could add a flag such as `unchanged: true` to the result and skip the toast, or show a neutral message instead.\n\n<!-- wachi:finding -->",
79	    "replies": [
80	      {
81	        "author": "csdev19",
82	        "body": "> [!NOTE]\n> 🤖 **Claude Sonnet 5.5 responding on behalf of Cristian Sotomayor**\n\nFixed in 392778fe: `relocateWorkspace` now returns `unchanged: true` when the picked folder is the one the workspace already uses. The IPC result carries it and the renderer skips the \"now points to the new folder\" toast, so nothing is shown. The test asserts the flag.\n"
83	      }

content.text: I've checked all seven earlier threads against the code and am now confirming whether the new `unchanged` path has renderer tests.

findings.title: No test covers skipping the toast when the folder is unchanged
findings.body:
The only check on the new flag is in `relocate.test.ts:158`, at the `relocateWorkspace` level. Two later steps have no test:
- `relocateFolder` copying `unchanged` into the IPC result (`index.ts:349`).
- The renderer skipping the "now points to the new folder" toast (`workspaces-context.tsx:168`).

`workspaces-settings.test.tsx:262` and `:282` already check that the toast appears after a real move. A matching case that resolves `relocate` with `{ ok: true, workspace, unchanged: true }` and expects `showToast` not to be called would keep the fix from regressing.

thread_replies.reply: Confirmed: the rollback now removes the identity written into a folder that had none (`registry.ts:645-646`).
Confirmed: name and color are checked separately, and a bad color now reports `invalid-color` (`index.ts:273-274`).
Confirmed: `edit` repeats the name check inside the locked `update` and undoes the identity write when that check fails (`registry.ts:626`, `:640-648`).

Confirmed for the case with no identity in the folder: `checkRelocate` now accepts it for a `pendingInit` entry (`registry.ts:855`). After an offline edit, `edit` keeps `pendingInit` (`registry.ts:634`), and the new test covers that. Adopting a folder that already holds another id is tracked as a follow-up, as you said.
Acknowledged as a follow-up. The relocate transaction still drops pending captures, so this stays open until that work lands.

Confirmed: when the picked folder is the current one, `relocateWorkspace` returns before `relocateActive` runs (`relocate.ts:43-45`). The test checks that the log is empty and the generation stays at 1.

Confirmed: `unchanged: true` travels from `relocate.ts:44` through `index.ts:349` to the renderer, which skips the toast (`workspaces-context.tsx:168`). Only the main-process side has a test; I left a separate note about testing the renderer side.

input.summary: This push fixes both items from the last round. When you pick the folder a workspace already uses, the result now carries `unchanged: true` and the renderer shows no \"now points to the new folder\" toast. An offline edit of a workspace that never got an `identity.json` keeps `pendingInit`, so Change folder… still accepts the moved folder. I found no defects. One optional suggestion: the renderer's skipped toast has no test. Six of the seven earlier threads are fixed in the current code; the pending-capture drop during a relocate is still open as an agreed follow-up.
